8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
11	
12	Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:
13	
14	- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
15	  applies to you.
16	- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
17	  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
18	  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
19	
20	## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference
21	
22	`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:
23	
24	- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
25	- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
26	  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
27	  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
28	- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
29	  materializing it is baselining's converge job, not yours.
30	- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
31	  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
32	  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.
33	
34	## 2. Arm auto-merge
35	
36	Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
37	it once this repo's required checks pass.
38	
39	## 3. When the arm is rejected
40	
41	- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
42	  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
43	  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
44	  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
45	  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
46	- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
47	  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
48	  PR's **head sha**:
49	  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
50	    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
51	  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
52	    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
53	  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
54	    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
55	    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
56	    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
57	    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
58	    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
59	    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
60	    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
61	    unseen check does not survive anything.
62	
63	## Never
64	
65	Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
66	arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
67	manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
68	are always legal outcomes.

# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; baselining re-derives the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '45 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=baselining.'
        required: false
        default: ''

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; baselining's deliver() pushes the maintenance branch (task-prework §7/E4)
  issues: write          # file / label / close dispatch issues
  pull-requests: write   # baselining's deliver() opens the per-cycle maintenance PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # read the run ledger (last successful run) for due-slot math, AND
                         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (store-release fires the release
                         # orchestrator's daily leg) — creating a workflow_dispatch event needs
                         # write, not read, and `read` silently 403s the POST

jobs:
  schedule:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Evaluate schedule and dispatch due tasks
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Empty on every scheduled run — `inputs` is only populated by
          # workflow_dispatch. The engine reads only FORCE_TASKS out of it.
          CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES: ${{ inputs.overrides }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue (DESIGN §3.6,
  # gha/scheduled-failure-escalation). Converges to ONE open issue by a fixed
  # title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a first-run
  # failure may precede the scheduler's own label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: schedule
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.

# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.

# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.

  schedule:
    - cron: '45 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=baselining.'

# Scheduled (and plain manual) runs serialize in one group so a slow run and its
# successor never overlap. A run carrying OVERRIDES gets a group of its own, keyed
# by run id: a forced run does exactly one named task, and the fleet fan-out case
# (an enforcer firing FORCE_TASKS at many members at once) must neither queue
# behind the hourly cron nor be silently dropped by it — GitHub keeps at most ONE
# pending run per group and cancels older pending ones, so a shared group can eat
# a forced dispatch without a trace. The (task, slot) exactly-once dispatch guard
# and the workers' idempotence are what make the rare overlap with a cron run safe.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler${{ inputs.overrides != '' && inputs.overrides != null && format('-forced-{0}', github.run_id) || '' }}

  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; baselining's deliver() pushes the maintenance branch (task-prework §7/E4)
